title: Shared/private skill bank with Mirror skill views
hypothesis: Two physical skill modules with per-skill Mirror Views will represent four logical skills and held-out skill combinations with at least 25% lower actual bytes than a four-module Polytropon bank, while keeping task NRMSE within 10%; private residuals should isolate off-orbit skills.
mirror_coordinate: per-logical-skill Givens angle selecting a view of one physical skill module
logical_multiplicity: four logical skills and sparse two-skill task compositions
controls: two physical modules with no Views
two physical modules plus skill Views
two modules plus one private residual for off-orbit skill

task.teacher: skills 0/1 are rotated views of module A; skill 2 is module B; skill 3 is off-orbit B+residual
task.tasks: all six pairwise skill combinations, with two held-out combination IDs
task.allocation: two sparse skill indices per task; same indices charged across controls

development.selection: fixed grid and support fit; no fresh tuning

paid_objects: skill matrices or shared physical matrices

success_gate: Every fresh world: Mirror NRMSE <=1.10x four-module bank on held-out pairwise tasks and N=6 payload <=75% four-module payload; report private residual crossover.
failure_gate: Mirror misses quality or byte gate, view gains are matched by simply increasing physical module count, or allocations fail to retain skill composition.
boundaries: Synthetic 2D skill bank only; no natural multi-task evidence.
The skill allocation IDs are supplied and equally charged.
One skill is deliberately off-orbit to measure private-state need.
amendment_A1: Initial fresh payload review found that the serialized four-module control carried the two-module skill_to_module map. Corrected the inference metadata before any result decision; original worlds 46810-46812 are retained as exploratory and excluded. A1 uses fresh world IDs.
